mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.5% consistently signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.5% indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects deteriorate.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) combined with restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) suppresses equity valuations through inflation control focus, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the regime condition.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 105 indicates robust manufacturing activity, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 105.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1100 thousand units signal housing sector contraction, reducing economic activity and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is below 1100.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment decline (PAYEMS) and unemployment rise (UNRATE) indicate labor market deterioration, depressing consumer confidence and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE increase fails to predict negative 20-day returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 105 indicates manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate profits and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 105.
